title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): K = Q^tr is the maximal totally real subfield of Q̄ ⊂ C. Write π = Gal(Q̄/Q) and τ for complex conjugation. Then π' = Gal(Q̄/K) is the closed normal subgroup generated by the conjugates τ_σ = στσ^{-1}. A is the maximal abelian extension of K, with H = Gal(A/K) = π'^{ab}. G = π/π' = Gal(K/Q) acts continuously on H by conjugation.

1) Structure of H. H is topologically generated by the G-translates σ·τ̇ of the image τ̇ of τ. These are involutions in an abelian group, so H is an elementary abelian pro-2 group. Equivalently, every abelian extension of Q^tr has exponent 2, i.e. is obtained by adjoining square roots.

2) Setup for the proposition. Let L be an abelian extension of K, Galois over Q, with L ≠ K. Its group Γ is then a G-equivariant nontrivial quotient of H. The following are equivalent:
(i) all στσ^{-1} (σ ∈ π) agree on L, hence agree with complex conjugation there;
(ii) [L:K] = 2 and L/Q is Galois;
(iii) L is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of K.
Moreover such an L exists and is unique: L = K·E for any imaginary quadratic field E, e.g. L = K(√-1).

3) Proof of (i) ⇔ (ii) and uniqueness. Under (i), Γ is generated by the single involution τ̇, so Γ ≅ Z/2Z. Since Aut(Z/2) is trivial, G acts trivially on Γ. Hence Γ is a quotient of the coinvariants H_G, which is generated by the single class of τ̇. Therefore Γ = H_G, which gives uniqueness, and L/Q is Galois. Conversely, (ii) gives Γ ≅ Z/2 generated by the images of the στσ^{-1}; these must all equal the unique nontrivial element, which is (i).

4) Proof of (ii) ⇔ (iii). For L quadratic over K: L totally imaginary ⇔ each στσ^{-1} acts nontrivially on L ⇔ each acts as the generator of Gal(L/K) ⇔ (i).

5) Purpose. The next page deduces that 𝕃 = Q^tr(i) is exactly the compositum Q^CM of all CM fields. Its subfields are precisely the totally real fields and the CM fields. It is also the largest Galois extension of Q in whose Galois group complex conjugation is central, and it contains Q^ab. This is the field of definition relevant to CM motives (later Serre group / Taniyama group) within the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' project.
errors: No mathematical error. The proof is terse but correct: H_G ≠ 0 follows from the existence of K(i), and Γ quotient of H_G uses that a Galois-over-Q quotient isomorphic to Z/2 must carry trivial G-action.
Small looseness: the sentence 'Donc il est annulé par 2' refers to H (generated by the involutions σ·τ̇), not to G. The machine transcription mistakenly makes G the subject ('commutatif').

ideas.what: Gal(Q̄/Q^tr) is normally generated by complex conjugation, so the maximal abelian extension of Q^tr has elementary abelian 2-group Galois group
ideas.modern_name: abelianization of the absolute Galois group of Q^tr (cf. 'real free' structure of G_{Q^tr})
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; full structure of G_{Q^tr} due to Fried–Haran–Völklein (1994) and Pop

ideas.what: Q^tr(√-1) is the unique quadratic extension of Q^tr that is Galois over Q; equivalently the unique totally imaginary quadratic extension of Q^tr
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in CM theory (Shimura–Taniyama; used by Serre 1968, Deligne 1979/82, Milne)

ideas.what: Characterization of Q^CM as the largest Galois extension of Q in which complex conjugation is central; its subfields are exactly totally real and CM fields (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Q^cm and the Serre group / CM motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968); Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct, but classical characterization of Q^CM = Q^tr(i) via the Galois group of Q^tr. It is an early appearance in Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes, foreshadowing the role of Q^cm in the Serre/Taniyama group, but the content is standard and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'qui est commutatif [?]' should read approximately 'qui opère continûment' (G acts continuously on H), and the following 'il' refers to H.
'σ_{τ̇}' denotes σ·τ̇, the G-translate of τ̇ in H.
'Soit L une extension abélienne de K, galoisienne sur Q, de Galois [i.e. de groupe] un quotient Γ de H' – the struck-out words are restored only partially in the transcription.
'élément τ̇ de degré [?] |2' should be read as 'élément τ̇ d'ordre |2' (order dividing 2).
Final line: '(ii),(ii) ⇔ (iii)' should be '(i),(ii) ⇔ (iii)', and 'on sait que' is more likely 'on suppose que' (L quadratic over K).
